corrected_value.title: Impact of a mentoring and skills group program on mental health outcomes for maltreated children in foster care.

decisions.quote: Fostering Healthy Futures (FHF) is a preventive PYD intervention for preadolescent children who have experienced maltreatment and placement in out-of-home care. It consists of individualized mentoring and weekly skills groups for 30 weeks. The conceptual and theoretical basis for FHF and anticipated proximal and distal effects are delineated elsewhere (cf. Taussig, Culhane & Hettleman, 2007 ). A pilot RCT with 156 youth found positive impacts on multi-informant (child, caregiver, teacher) reports of mental health functioning (including trauma symptoms), mental health services, and quality of life ( Taussig & Culhane, 2010 ).
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly aims to replicate and extend the mental health findings of the pilot FHF RCT cited as Taussig & Culhane (2010) (DOI: 10.1001/archpediatrics.2010.124) in the text and reference list. The shipped row pointed to an uncited 2012 conference abstract (Taussig, 2012; 10.1037/e522512014-027) instead of the cited primary published trial article.

decisions.quote: Intervention youth scored significantly lower on the mental health index ( β = −.11; t = −2.32; p < .05), posttraumatic stress symptoms ( β = −.09; t = −2.01; p < .05) and dissociation scales ( β = −.12; t = −2.76; p < .01), and they were less likely to be receiving mental health treatment at T2 (B = −.47; Wald = 4.43; p =.04). Intervention and control groups did not differ on quality of life or psychotropic medication use.
decisions.reason: Resolving the dependent original identity to Taussig & Culhane (2010), the paper states that the pilot RCT found positive impacts on three domains: multi-informant mental health functioning (including trauma symptoms), mental health services, and quality of life. In the replication, FHF significantly reduced mental health problems (mental health index, posttraumatic stress, and dissociation) and mental health treatment utilization, confirming the first two pilot findings, but found no main effect difference between intervention and control groups on quality of life. Because the Discussion confirms the specific effects on mental health symptomatology and service utilization rather than stating an overall replication verdict that all pilot findings held, codebook Rule 2 governs and the mix of confirmed and unconfirmed original findings yields 'mixed'.

decisions.quote: The current study sought to replicate and extend the mental health findings of the pilot FHF trial by adding data from five additional cohorts ( N =270) as well as examine moderating effects.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding agree that the study is a replication: it collected new data from five additional cohorts (N = 270) pooled with the five pilot cohorts to re-test the published mental health findings of the pilot FHF trial (Taussig & Culhane, 2010).
